A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same information-locality-based RTL generation framework, renamed from LocalV to ChipV-RTL. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. v2 retains Appendices A-F and adds Appendix G.

before.justification: v1 reports original REALBENCH and CVDP evaluations, locality measurements, ablations, retrieval assessments, and hardware PPA results, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and reports additional baseline scores and revised VerilogCoder results in Table 3.

M1.justification: The preprocessing, planning, localized generation, merging, and AST-guided debugging procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. Renaming the framework and disclosing parameters do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Coverage remains REALBENCH's 60 module tasks, CVDP cid003, and the same concatenated VerilogEval and Parse Lisp Expression locality cases. No dataset, domain, or task scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds evaluated DeepRTL2 and VeriReason-3B baselines on REALBENCH while retaining the existing comparators. Spec2RTL and RTLSquad are added to the architectural comparison in Table 1, without corresponding experimental scores.

E3.justification: v2 documents reduced-cost VerilogCoder limits, approximately one-tenth of defaults, and MAGE candidate settings selected for comparable token budgets. v1 supplies no corresponding limits, so the PDFs do not establish whether these protocols changed or were newly disclosed. Tasks, metrics, and stated generation counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, indexing sensitivity, error breakdowns, debugging-efficiency analysis, PPA comparisons, and workflow/failure/locality case studies are retained. Tables 4-6 and Appendices B-F provide the same analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 independent generations per task for direct-prompting baselines and a single generation for agent baselines. No additional seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces VerilogCoder's overall 0.0% syntactic/functional scores with 36.6%/20.0%, and adds DeepRTL2 and VeriReason-3B overall functional scores of 2.3% and 4.1%. Section 4.2 newly reports approximately threefold token consumption for VerilogCoder relative to ChipV-RTL. Protocol comparability for the replaced scores is unresolved; the proposed method's results and existing analyses remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, information-locality assumption, and relevance/probability/normalized-entropy definitions in Equations 1-5 are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or mathematical correction is added.

C1.justification: The conclusion newly calls ChipV-RTL the first open-source framework towards IP-level design automation; v1 described a tailored multi-agent framework without this priority claim. The locality contribution and headline performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the interpretation that VerilogCoder fails completely with a qualified discussion of its reduced-cost configuration, remaining token overhead, and lower correctness. The introduction adds an explanation of debugging difficulty through interactions among specifications, interfaces, and submodules. Existing failure limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix G and Table 7 substantially expand reproducibility documentation with temperatures, top-p, retry limits, vLLM version, and MAGE/VerilogCoder candidate and conversation limits, alongside budget-selection explanations. The abstract also adds code/project access information. These are documented disclosures; they do not establish that every listed setting changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds the VeriReason citation and expands Table 1's architectural positioning to Spec2RTL and RTLSquad. It acknowledges prior debugging work and replaces categorical criticism of earlier models with uncertainty about their IP-level scalability. The conclusion also introduces the open-source priority claim.

P1.justification: The framework is renamed throughout, front matter is updated, and selected introduction, related-work, results, and conclusion passages are revised. Acknowledgment, Impact Statement, and Appendix G are added; the main organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains comparator columns and revised feature rows, Table 3 gains two baseline rows, and Table 7 is new. Existing figures retain their content, with updated method labels and changes in placement and surrounding page layout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through Appendix G and access information, broadens evaluated comparisons, and replaces the categorical VerilogCoder failure account with quantified results and budget explanations. These provide useful, limited gains while the central method and supporting analyses remain stable. The earlier baseline budgets remain unspecified, and the new first-open-source claim cannot be established from the supplied PDFs alone.
